catalog_quote: 2.4 Tone. As evidenced by minimal pairs such as ... ‘sacrifice’ vs. ... ‘calf’ or ... ‘girl’ vs. ‘Fula’, Ganja has a tone system relying on a H vs. L contrast. There are also a rising and a falling tone, analyzable as LH and HL sequences associated to single syllables, and a downstep, analyzable as manifesting the presence of a floating L tone. The floating L tones may result from phonological processes, as illustrated in (1b), or may be part of the underlying form of some morphemes (for example the nominal prefixes b- and g-). As regards the functional load of tone, minimal pairs are not very numerous in the lexicon, and all verbs have the same lexical tone, but tone plays an important role in verbal morphology. ... 6.1.1 Tonal properties of verbal lexemes. The verbal lexemes of Ganja have no inherent tone, and the tone of verb stems is entirely determined by the grammatical nature of …

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Quote verified verbatim at the stated preprint pages (7, 27, 45) of the held Creissels OUP sketch; zero 'stress'/'accent' tokens in that text. The deciding source is a 2024 handbook sketch, but it is by the language's principal describer, and the underlying 370-pp reference grammar (Creissels & Biaye 2016, Glottolog's top grammar for bala1302) is openly posted on the author's site; I downloaded it to Its phonology chapter has consonants, vowels, tones (binary H/B, contour tones as BH/HB on one syllable, downstep, floating L), syllable structure and liaison, with no stress/accent section and no prosodic use of 'accent' anywhere in the book: it confirms the 'tonal, no word stress described' coding exactly. The grammar also notes Fudeman 1999 ignores tone and describes a semi-speaker, so no competing English source is likely to overturn this.

sources.note: Sec. 4 'Prosodie' (p.3) states a tone system with a binary opposition haut vs bas, proven by minimal pairs sádá 'sac' / sàdá 'veau' and àfúlá 'fille' / àfúlà 'Peul'; rising and falling contour tones (fɟǎ: 'la langue balante', mfʊ̂l 'grenouille') analysed as L-H and H-L sequences on one syllable. The sheet says nothing about downstep and nothing about the role of tone in the verbal system (those points are in the 2016 grammar, not here); S's gloss of sádá as 'veau' was also off (sádá = 'sac', sàdá = 'veau'). Quote (p.3): 'Le balante ganja a un système tonal reposant sur une opposition binaire…

sources.note: READ (full text of the review in the open-access LLA 3 issue PDF; extract kept). Secondary statement, p.120: 'En ce qui concerne les tons, les auteurs stipulent que le balant ganja n’a que deux tons de base, H et B, et analysent les occurrences de tons moyens de surface comme le résultat de plusieurs règles d’abaissement tonal (downdrift) et de faille tonale (downstep).
